A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeshPad and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The retained content can be matched despite changes in terminology, formatting, and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeNet and IKEA experiments, mesh-editing evaluations, speculator ablations, runtime measurements, and a 35-participant perceptual study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and additionally reports topology measurements, sketch-alignment examples, and qualitative editing results after fine-tuning on two further datasets.

M1.justification: The addition/deletion decomposition, OPT networks, RADIO encoder, mesh tokenizer, losses, and jointly trained vertex-aligned speculator are retained. The revised architecture diagram and Appendix A explain existing components; the additional dataset fine-tuning does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E and Figure 13 add fine-tuning and qualitative editing on Objaverse and meshes sampled from DeformingThings4D animations, extending coverage to broader objects and articulated animal/human shapes. ShapeNet, IKEA, and the 50-shape editing set remain. Image conditioning and editing externally supplied meshes were already demonstrated in v1.

E2.justification: LAS, LAS-MA, SENS, and SENS-MA remain the evaluated comparison methods. The new topology analysis uses this same set, with training meshes as an additional reference. Updated LAS scores and newly documented input handling do not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: New appendix experiments introduce topology metrics and fine-tuning setups using approximately 9,000 filtered Objaverse meshes and 1,000 sampled, decimated DeformingThings4D meshes. Existing splits, training budgets, and perceptual-study design remain unchanged. Newly specified timing and baseline-input procedures are disclosures, without sufficient evidence that those procedures changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantive structural-quality analysis comparing face counts, components, non-manifold edges, and self-intersections with baselines and training data. Figure 12 also tests sketch-size sensitivity, interior edits, and connecting added geometry. Existing speculator ablations, nearest-neighbor analysis, and interactive-versus-single-step comparisons are retained, including relocated material.

E5.justification: The perceptual-rating standard deviations in v1 Table 5 are retained in v3 Table 6, together with the same participant and task counts. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new topology descriptors do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise LAS and LAS-MA results: LAS Chamfer distance changes from 22.46 to 15.02 on ShapeNet and 20.69 to 16.27 on IKEA. Identical LAS conditions across versions are not established, so these are revised reports rather than demonstrated same-setting gains. Table 4 changes the no-joint-training speed from 125.3 to 130.8 tokens/s. New topology and fine-tuning results substantially expand the evidence, and some Figure 11 examples are replaced. MeshPad's main benchmark scores and perceptual-study results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds an explicit mathematical construction of triangle chains from consecutive vertex triples in Equation 7, where v1 only described the adopted adjacent-triangle tokenization. The editing, speculator, and volume-sampling equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: localized sketch-driven addition/deletion and vertex-aligned acceleration. The headline claims of over 22% Chamfer-distance improvement, approximately 90% perceptual preference, and 2.2× acceleration are unchanged. The title's terminology change does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that exact sketch-to-mesh alignment is not guaranteed. Appendix F interprets reduced self-intersections as possibly reflecting simpler learned surface representations. The existing novelty example is newly interpreted as synthesis beyond training categories, and the context-length discussion now proposes token compression.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information through tokenization/traversal details, explicit separation of network weights, first-300-token timing, LAS category restrictions and camera/preprocessing inputs, and SENS checkpoint selection. It also documents new fine-tuning data preparation and supplies a project-page link. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained method or resource availability beyond the stated link.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Free2CAD, MeshXL, LLMLingua, Objaverse, and 4DComplete, extending discussion of CAD representations, context-length limitations, and additional datasets. The main positioning around editable explicit meshes and speculative decoding remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Terminology and several explanatory passages are refined, including the title's change to 'Artist-Reminiscent.' Sketch-generation details, interface implementation, and the complex-shape comparison are regrouped into lettered appendices. Most existing prose and the main argument's section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document undergoes extensive visual reformatting. The full-page comparison becomes compact paired generation/editing columns, the sequence montage is rearranged and loses its airplane sequence, and Figure 3 is redrawn to distinguish the networks. Figures 12–13 and the topology table are added, while existing figures and tables are relocated and recaptioned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability and reproducibility through clearer technical specifications, useful topology diagnostics, and an explicit sketch-alignment limitation, while retaining the principal supporting results. The gains remain limited: the new-domain evidence consists of qualitative fine-tuning examples, and the reported baseline averages use different category subsets. These additions strengthen the paper without resolving its broader validation limitations.
